title: Friday Sermon 66: God's Greatness, Human Idols, Food Prohibitions, and Righteousness (1982-12-10)
source_file: data/sources/playlists/audio-transcripts/66 - Friday Sermon 10 Dec. 1982 By Dr Rashad Khalifa.csv
document_summary: Rashad's sermon begins with the human function of worshiping God alone and an extended cosmic comparison intended to show God's greatness and the insignificance of human idols. Jesus, Mary, Muhammad, and all messengers are described as people who ate food and walked in markets. Rashad promises kingship, security, and protection to God-alone believers and tells a self-harm survival anecdote. The second sermon reports letters from India, mass printing of Quran-code summaries, Arabic lessons, and a debate over keeping birth names, adopted children, and so-called slave names. After prayer, participants discuss the Bible and Paul, then study Quran 2:168–179. The long food block rejects inherited prohibitions, vegetarianism as religion, elaborate Jewish and Muslim food restrictions, Hadith-based bans on pig-derived products, and limits the forbidden foods to carrion, pork meat, running blood, and offerings dedicated to other than God. The recording ends with Quran 2:177's definition of righteousness and the opening of the capital-punishment discussion.

related_duplicate_sources.note: Both sermons use cosmic and bodily scale to attack human idolatry.
Study 65 ends at Quran 2:167 and this recording continues with 2:168.
Study 67 continues the Quran 2:178–182 legal discussion.

content_guidance.rule: Separate the two sermons from the post-prayer study
content_guidance.instruction: The recording changes genre around thirty minutes.
Rashad himself labels it personal opinion.
It is not evidence of survivability or protection.

sections.title: Cosmic greatness, prophets who eat food, the insignificance of idols, and promised protection
sections.summary: Rashad compares Earth, the solar system, the Milky Way, stars, and vast distances with the smallness of human figures. Quran 5:75, 21:8, and 25:7 and 20 emphasize that Jesus, Mary, and all messengers ate food and walked in markets. He says God-alone believers will become kings or queens, suffer no bad event, and tells of a relative who survived a gunshot to the head after attempting suicide.

sections.title: Letters from India, million-copy distributions, Arabic lessons, original names, adoption, and slave-name objections
sections.summary: Rashad says the God-alone message is spreading through a correspondent in India and two million-copy printings in Egypt. He announces Quran-based Arabic lessons. He then argues, as a stated personal opinion, that people and adopted children should retain their original names. Participants raise adoption, marriage between unknown siblings, women's surnames, and the objection that African American surnames were inherited from slaveholders.

sections.title: Quran 2:168–173, lawful food, ancestral prohibitions, vegetarianism, pork, and necessity
sections.summary: Quran 2:168–173 commands lawful food and warns against following ancestral customs and inventing prohibitions. Participants discuss animal sounds, strict vegetarianism as a religious rule, Hindu and Southeast Asian restrictions, Jewish food practice, pork, and the exemption for necessity without malicious intent.
related_questions: How were ancestral and vegetarian restrictions criticized?
sections.canonical_text: These verses here in 165, 166, 167 are identical to Matthew 7:23. Free mind, prerequisite for salvation. Dr. Khalifa: Dean Mahmoud would you, if you like. Dean Mahmoud: Bism Allah Arrahman Arraheem [2:168] O people, eat from everything that is lawful and good, and do not follow the steps of Satan; he is your ardent enemy. [2:169] He directs you towards vice and evil, and to invent lies and attribute them to God. [2:170] When they are told, "Follow only God's commandments," they say, "We follow what we found our parents doing." What if their parents lack the understanding and guidance? [2:171] The example of such disbelievers is that of a parrot; they repeat what they heard without understanding. Deaf, dumb, and blind; they fail to understand. [2:172] O you who believe, eat from the good things we provide for you, and be thankful to GOD, if you do worship Him alone. [2:173] He only prohibits for you animals that die of themselves (without human interference), blood, the meat of pigs, and animals sacrificed in any name other than GOD. However, if one is forced (to eat these), without being malicious or deliberate, then he incurs no sin. GOD is Forgiver, Merciful. [2:174] Those who conceal God's revelations in the scripture, seeking a lowly material gain, are eating fire into their bellies. GOD will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He sanctify them. They will suffer painful retribution. [2:175] It is they who chose the straying instead of guidance, and the retribution instead of forgiveness. Consequently, they will have to endure Hell fire. [2:176] That is because GOD has sent down this scripture truthfully, and those who dispute the scripture are in manifest defiance. Well, I don't know what I can say about, this is so, so clear. Actually, as Muslims we can conclude from what I've read that aside from those things that are prohibited any rule adding certain foods and so on made by human beings without authority from Allah are in the long run the work of Satan himself. And this is found all over the world. I know, as a matter of fact, that in, in India and Pakistan, especially among the Hanafi madhhab (sect), they do not eat shrimps, they do not eat lobsters, they do not eat crabs. Dean Mahmoud: Well, they're missing something. Dr. Khalifa: That's for sure. Dean Mahmoud: And also, this idea of the holiness of certain animals like cows and so on, in the long run this is not helping many, many people. I can imagine that due to doctor's order maybe meat, too much meat might be bad for certain people especially if they reach, reach a certain age. But in India, I've seen, I've been in India maybe 10, 15 times, I've seen cows go to the marketplace. They're not at all touched, they wander, they walk among the people, and these cows have very long tongues. When they see vegetables, you know, they stick out their tongues and then drop all the food, and no one harms any cows, they just pull them gently, which is nice in some ways, to see how people are gentle to animals. Dean Mahmoud: But the seller becomes poorer. Dean Mahmoud: And... Dr. Khalifa: The cow doesn't pay, does he? Dean Mahmoud: Not at all. Dean Mahmoud: But if a human being steals one, one Bazenjan (باذنجان), what's called (unintelligible), one egg plant, they pull, they beat him up and so on. I, I think that this is... I don't know who invented this, strict vegetarianism as a religious, as a religious rule. Anyhow, in Southeast Asia, we have a lot of prohibitions, too. Dean Mahmoud: May I add also, among some Hanafis, they will not eat these, what is Khiyar (خیار)? Dr. Khalifa: Oh, cucumber? Dean Mahmoud: They will not eat cucumbers that are slightly bitter because of a Hadith which says that the prophet once ate it and he said, "it's too bitter." Dean Mahmoud: So,... A man: (unintelligible) Dean Mahmoud: Now, this is an addition. There are some Hadiths that prohibit extra food and so on. And this forces a lot of wastage of natural resources. But, now, how about this? Some food that is good, but it just happened that it was dedicated to an idol. Dean Mahmoud: Well, this is a, this is a prohibit also because it involves, I think, the principle of shirk or idol worship. Dr. Khalifa: Permission from the Creator. Dean Mahmoud: Yeah, if... I would like also to mention something very interesting. You don't have it in the States, but I've traveled a lot. There are some Chinese who embrace Islam. And they get the picture of their father and they put it on the wall. And they have beautiful fruits, apples, imported because we don't have these in our country, Dean Mahmoud: apples, oranges, and they put these... Dr. Khalifa: In front of their pictures. Dean Mahmoud: in front of their pictures and they, they bow down to the picture of their parents and so on. Dr. Khalifa: They do this to Santa Claus, they leave cookies and milk. Dean Mahmoud: But this basically is what you call ancestral, ancestor worship, but it's a transition. These are sometimes it's, one cannot be very hard on this, a new convert to Islam, because they are passing through a transition or transitory period from a form of "paganism" to Islam. And, but I personally think it's a waste of good food, put it in the picture of a dead father or grandfather and so on. And in some ways, it is even possible that this falls under this rule, that they have been offered to, in the name of someone else besides Allah. And the thinking of some of the 'ulama in our country is that the fact that these fruits are offered to a dead ancestor and has not been offered to Allah Himself, Dean Mahmoud: being a form of ancestral, Dr. Khalifa: Paganist. Dean Mahmoud: a kind of pagan worship, Dean Mahmoud: the 'ulama says, just convince the old men not to put those fruits to all of us (unintelligible). And we were successful in convincing some of these Chinese and so on. But I think the, the question is the matter of symbolism. This is the uncompromising monotheism of, of Islam. However, I think personally, it's just an opinion. If one is in danger of starvation, then maybe without having the intention of a transgression, as the imam Al-Ghazali says, between two evils, starving and eating a little pork to live, in order to pray better (unintelligible), once, once the starvation is through, these are two evils. Dean Mahmoud: We have to choose the Dr. Khalifa: Lesser evil. Dean Mahmoud: the lesser, lesser evil. In other cases, it's not deliberate. We know, as a matter of fact, that when we, Muftis, travel, and people know this happens in, in Asia, especially among Christians, they know that we are Muslims, and we tell them we cannot eat pork, "Yes", they say, "yes", you know, as a matter of fact that they sometimes make fun. They throw a piece of pork. That's done in the army. I know this piece has been brought to my attention. Among soldiers, they put a piece of pork and give it to the Muslims and say, "this is very good, it has no pork." And when the Muslim said, "oh, this is very nice food", then they all laugh behind their back. Dean Mahmoud: Now, there is no sin for these Muslims. Dr. Khalifa: Right. Dean Mahmoud: But it is very, very malicious. And I say, the harm is not upon the Muslim who is innocent. It's among those who are, who are malicious. And there is no, nothing, there's no sin in it. And Quran says this very clear. [2:173] ... without being malicious or deliberate, then he incurs no sin. ... Well, I can't mention the other verses that may discuss, you can help us here, that it appears that for some time, the Jews were prohibited from certain kinds of foods as a kind of discipline, or punishment from Allah. I think you'll remember this is, we discussed this. But it's very interesting because the Quran mentions that when Christ came, Dean Mahmoud: he said that one need not follow God Dr. Khalifa: (unintelligible) Dean Mahmoud: anymore. A man: (unintelligible) Dean Mahmoud: I cannot, I don't have my notes with me. A man: (unintelligible). Dean Mahmoud: But, it is very interesting, sister Laila was showing me a, a recipe, of chicken liver. Now, this is very interesting. I hope I'm not, this, this seems like gossiping, but it will show us certain insight. Sister Maryam gave me a recipe, wherein you can mix chicken liver with chicken heart. But, in the Jewish recipe, they, they used butter, although that comes from an animal. In other words, the Jews. Dean Mahmoud: never fry meat with oil or fat of the same animal. Dr. Khalifa: I see. Dean Mahmoud: The Jews will not boil meat with milk. This is haram to them. The Jews will not fry meat with cow's fat or with chicken fat. They'll use olive oil or vegetable oil. The Jews also will not eat food that is combined, like chicken meat and lamb. They don't combine. Or beef and lamb. No, it must be only one of a kind. In other words, it has become very, very neurotic. And we know that there is a law in, in society, unlike the proverb that says that a rolling stone gathers no moss. But in society it's different. As a social institution grows older, it begins to acquire more moss. These are the barnacles, like the ship. When a ship travels longer, it acquires more barnacles. And social institutions gather more and more barnacles. And so, these religious prohibitions become more and more and more involved. Dean Mahmoud: And this is what is happening to Islam. Dr. Khalifa: Yeah. Dean Mahmoud: Without permission from Allah Himself. 169 says, [2:169] He directs you towards vice, ... That is the devil. And devil also makes us invent lies. Dean Mahmoud: and attribute them to, to God. Dr. Khalifa: Exactly. Dean Mahmoud: So, our 'ulama, either they're not thinking well, and sometimes they're not really malicious,

sections.title: Religious barnacles, Hadith restrictions, pig products, the four forbidden foods, commercial meat, Bismillah, and blood
sections.summary: Dean compares accumulating religious restrictions with barnacles on an old ship.
